item.title: LOT-073: review leftovers (superEncoder, nits)
item.body:
LOT-073
Refs #97 (follow-up of #490's review leftovers; nothing else left on #97)
Claim: ext/francoisgn-opus-2
Author model: Opus 5.5

**Problem.** Fable's adversarial review of #490 (merged as 501d1be) left three items:
1. **Low**: `JSONTreeEncoder`'s `superEncoder()` (keyed and unkeyed parents) wrote `{}` when the super encoded a single value or an unkeyed container; `JSONEncoder` writes the value (`{"super":1,"x":2}`). No `HFRModels` type uses `superEncoder` today, so no stored document was affected.
2. **Nit**: `JSONTreeNode.count` returned 1 for a `.value` node (and the member count for an object); only array nodes are asked.
3. **Nit**: `JSONTreeEncoder.claim` silently replaces a node of another kind where `JSONEncoder` traps.

**Cause.** The super encoder was given an empty-object placeholder node already set in the parent; it was reused only when the super asked for a keyed container, so a value or an array replaced the child's node and the parent kept the placeholder.

**Change.**
- `JSONTreeNode.Content.deferred(JSONTreeEncoder)`: the parent holds the super's encoder and reads its node when the tree is finished (`{}` if it wrote nothing, as before). Both super-encoder sites use it; no placeholder any more.
- `count` answers for array nodes only (0 otherwise), with a comment on why.
- `claim` documents the intended difference from `JSONEncoder` (replace instead of trap: only a malformed `encode(to:)` hits it, and the app should not crash on it). No behaviour change.

Nothing else touched; no public API change.

**Tests.** `JSONWriterTests.superEncoders(shape:)` (parameterised: single value, unkeyed, keyed super) encodes a type through `superEncoder()`, `superEncoder(forKey:)` and an unkeyed `superEncoder()`, and compares with `JSONEncoder`'s text. Without the fix the `.single` and `.unkeyed` cases fail (`Expectation failed: text == (try Self.foundation(value))`); with it all pass. Full suite on Linux (Swift 6.2.4): 1497 tests green; `check-lot-deps.py` 0 violations.

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Claude Fable 5.1, `ext/francoisgn-fable-review-5`, independent of the author): APPROVE** — head 964feb296bbdd516951cc6eb9052e52d6cab26a7

No High or Medium findings. The deferred node reproduces `JSONEncoder`'s `__JSONReferencingEncoder` write-back (value / array / object kept; an untouched super written as `{}`) and is read only when the tree is finished, so late writes through a kept super land.

1. **Low** — `Packages/HFRKit/Sources/HFRModels/MPStorage/JSONTreeEncoder.swift:153,177-181`: after `list.superEncoder()` the tree counts the deferred node at once (`count` 2 after `[1, super]`), while Foundation's unkeyed container counts it only at deinit (`count` 1, and the next item's `codingPath` index repeats the super's). Probe: encode `1`, super, `2`, `3`: both write `[1,["s"],2,3]`, so only the index seen *during* encoding (errors' `codingPath`, `count`) differs, and nothing in HFRKit/App calls `superEncoder`. No fix needed; a one-line note in the `claim`/`superEncoder` comment would record the chosen (saner) convention.
2. **Nit** — PR body: `Direct-PR:` together with `Refs #97` and no `Claim:` line mixes AGENTS §8's two forms, and §8 says `Direct-PR` is never for a lot while the commit is titled `LOT-073: …`. Keep `Refs #97` + `Claim:` (or `Direct-PR` alone, labelled `direct-pr`).

**Checked**
- `swift test` on the head: 137 tests / 13 suites green on Swift 6.2.4 Linux; no warnings in the touched files; diff lines ≤ 140.
- LESSONS 2: PR's test run against the `origin/dev-swift` sources fails `.single` and `.unkeyed` (passes `.keyed`); mutating `.deferred` to resolve as `{}` fails all three shapes; head passes all.
- Own probes against Foundation (`.sortedKeys`): untouched supers (`super`, keyed, in a list) → `{}` matches; super mid-list with later items matches; super-in-super (two deferrals) matches; a super written after another key matches; `Double.nan` through a super throws `EncodingError.invalidValue` with `codingPath == ["bad"]`.
- `JSONTreeNode.count` now array-only: `Unkeyed` is the only caller and always holds an array node; no `.deferred` node ever becomes an encoder's own node, so `isSameKind`/`claim` are unaffected.
- No retain cycle: parent node → child encoder → child's own node. No Sendable crossing: both classes internal, non-Sendable, used on one task.
- Boundaries: `HFRModels` only, Foundation-only, no I/O, no network, no state-changing request, no cookies/tokens; spec LOT-073 makes no claim about super encoders, so no doc drift. No fixtures touched.
- LESSONS rows 1–56 walked; none else apply (no HFR facts, no captures, no concurrency with sessions).
